Guidance & outlook: See, in the next year our target is INR25 lakhs for the whole of MOIL.
But definitely next year's target is 25 lakhs and we are working on that.

And for the next year our c apex is target is around INR800 crores, because INR400 crores around INR350 crores would be having for the modernization of our mines and the remaining would be for the overseas acquisition.
Growth & demand: As per th e last published data, MOIL holds around 20% of the India's manganese resources, through which it meets the company's 50% demand.
MOIL contributes around 50% of the market share and it holds around 18% market share.
MOIL is increasing its market share from 20% to around 32% by 2030.
Margins & costs: And last year, that is '24-'25 our cost of production was around, that is for manganese ore, was at the fact -- because our cost of production the factory gate was around INR5,500 per ton and this year would be around 53 something so there will be reduction in the cost of production.
So the cost of production will go down because at the moment the biggest portion of our cost of production is our manpower, which is almost around 48% something.

But what is important is that the things that we are doing now, I just explained about the mechanization, the employee count going down, this would be beneficial, in fact, the impact of the wage negotiation wage revision would not be felt that much, because what is happening now we had a very static production, then after some time we took a very huge jump, …
Capex & expansion: So in 1962, Government of India took over from CPMO and acquired 51% stake.
In the current year, we have envisaged around INR325 crores of capex investment for capacity enhancement, modernization, and mechanization of our mines.
As far as capex plan is concerned, last year our capex we achieved was INR321 crores.
Balance sheet & cash: Also, we have declared two interim dividends during the financial year.
First interim dividend was of INR1.80 an d second interim dividend was of INR3.53.
Risks & challenges: Your presentation states a similar number for this particular year that is roughly 23.6 lakhs for FY '26, which I believe is going to be a big, big challenge considering the first 9 months was only 1.4.
So there's a little delay and that's why this 23.5 lakhs could not be achieved, okay.
So that's another reason why off late, if you have seen the prices in last two weeks, this Friday it was not so volatile, previous Friday prices shot up by almost 6%.

Guidance & outlook: This year, we have targeted 20% more compared to last year, and we are very much sure that we will achieve it.
And this year, we have took a target of 66% more from this year, which will definitely help us to enhance the production.
So that is why we are confident that unless something -- I mean, something that big happens, which is beyond our control, we are confident we'll be touching more than 1.7 million ton this year.
Growth & demand: MOIL has achieved best ever 6 monthly productions in April to September 2023, and that is 8.15 lakh million -- metric ton, registering a significant growth of 45% over corresponding period last year.
Third thing is that the company has also recorded best -ever 6-monthly sales performance at 7.57 lakh tons during April to September '23, registering a growth of 54% over CPLY.

And when we met last time, I said it will be double -digit growth, but now I'm confident it will be around 28% to 30% growth we'll be achieving over the previous year, which was the second highest perf ormance since inception.
Margins & costs: And we are definitely with same inputs, same resources, we have increased our production 45% more.
See, the best EBITDA we achieved in a few years back was around 45%.
Our cost is only increasing -- when we achieved 45% of growth in production, our cost has increased only by 5%.
Capex & expansion: Last year, we did a capex of INR245 crores, which is near to our PAT.
And about the production capacity, as I have mentioned even in last Investor Meet that very first year, we expect 0.2 million ton and then subsequently...
So that we got and our capacity has increased from 1.8 lakh tons to 4 lakh tons.
